How it works

Home-based means no storefront to visit — everything is by appointment.

1

Message me

Tell me what's wrong, or what you'd like built. Plain words are fine — you don't need the technical terms.

2

Drop it off

Drop your computer off at the agreed time. No storefront, no queue — just knock and hand it over.

3

Get a firm price first

You get a clear price before any work begins. No work goes ahead without you saying yes to it.

4

Pick it up, fixed

Collect your computer working again, with everything explained in plain language.

About

One person. No shop overhead. No upsell.

I've been building computers since 2015 — gaming rigs for friends and family, work machines, and plenty of “it's just slow now” rescues in between. Stoehr Computer Services is that same work, done properly as a local St. Catharines business.

Because there's no storefront and no staff to cover, you're not paying for a shop on top of the job. You deal with the same person from the first message to pick-up, and I'll tell you honestly when an upgrade isn't worth it and a replacement makes more sense.

What helps me quote faster

For a problem: what the computer is doing (or not doing), any warning messages you see, and whether it's a laptop or desktop.

For a build: what you'll use it for, the games or programs you run, and a rough budget for parts.

For an upgrade: roughly how old the machine is, and what feels slow.
